A normal BP does not exclude shock?
cards.b: POD 2 after low anterior resection, lactate rising 2.2 → 4.7 despite 2 L, BP 108/68 → compensated shock; rising lactate means persistent hypoperfusion — look for bleeding, sepsis, bowel ischaemia, cardiac dysfunction, mixed shock.

cards.f: MAP is a target, not proof?
cards.b: septic shock with MAP 70 on norepinephrine but mottled, oliguric, rising lactate → reassess macro/microcirculation, cardiac output, fluid responsiveness, source control. Capillary refill, skin, lactate trend, urine output and mental state all count.

cards.f: Most accurate marker of inadequate tissue perfusion → lactate; best monitor of adequate resuscitation
MAP = DBP + ⅓(SBP − DBP): BP 80/50

SIRS: HR 110, RR 25, T 38.5, WBC 13,000 with normal BP → SIRS; HR is a SIRS criterion; T 38.4 + WBC 14,000 supports SIRS; organ dysfunction

cards.b: insulin resistance and ↑ glucagon (keys differ: 434 = glucagon, 433 = insulin)

Haemorrhagic/hypovolaemic — Clues from the lecture cases?
cards.b: Cool peripheries, narrow pulse pressure, falling Hb, abdominal distension, positive FAST

cards.f: Distributive (septic) — Clues from the lecture cases?
cards.b: Warm peripheries, bounding pulses, low systemic vascular tone (early)

cards.f: Cardiogenic — Clues from the lecture cases?
cards.b: Crackles, raised JVP, cool peripheries after fluid in IHD

cards.f: Obstructive — Clues from the lecture cases?
cards.b: Tension pneumothorax (absent breath sounds, distended neck veins); PE (dilated RV, septal flattening); tamponade

cards.f: Mixed — Clues from the lecture cases?
cards.b: Common in surgical patients — never use one sign alone to exclude haemorrhage or sepsis

cards.f: Persistent shock after initial resuscitation needs phenotyping?
cards.b: dynamic fluid-responsiveness tests and focused echocardiography (persistent preload responsiveness, vasoplegia, ventricular dysfunction, tamponade, right-heart strain). Static indices like CVP alone are unreliable.

cards.f: Vasopressors?
cards.b: norepinephrine can run through a good peripheral line temporarily — don't delay it for central access.

cards.f: Arterial line?
cards.b: beat-to-beat pressure and repeated blood sampling in unstable shock/vasopressor use — it doesn't measure volume or replace examination.

cards.f: Tension pneumothorax
Hypotension + bradycardia + warm extremities after trauma (spinal injury)
Anterior MI with BP 80/50 (cardiogenic shock) → normal intravascular volume ; chest pain + hypotension POD 1
Anaphylaxis to IV contrast (bradycardia, hypotension)
Collapse in recovery 1 h after appendectomy
cards.b: hypovolemic shock (bleeding) ; bleeding, aspiration and PE are causes — wound abscess is NOT (too early)

cards.f: Tachycardia + low urine output after sleeve gastrectomy
Concealed bleeding?
cards.b: hypotension 6 h after lap chole, Hb 12.6 → 8.8, distension, drain only 30 mL → concealed intra-abdominal haemorrhage — drains can block or not communicate. Treat as haemorrhage until proved otherwise.

cards.f: Lethal cycle?
cards.b: hypothermia + acidosis + coagulopathy + hypocalcaemia (T 34, pH 7.16, low ionised Ca) = trauma-induced coagulopathy → haemorrhage control, warming, balanced products, calcium, minimal crystalloid.

cards.f: Damage-control resuscitation?
cards.b: avoid large crystalloid volumes (dilute clotting factors, worsen hypothermia/acidosis, dislodge clots); permissive hypotension is NOT for traumatic brain injury.

cards.f: TBI + haemorrhagic shock?
cards.b: prevent hypoxaemia and hypotension (protect cerebral perfusion) while doing damage-control haemorrhage management; brief hyperventilation only as rescue; mannitol/hypertonic not routinely.

cards.f: Warfarin with active bleeding and instability
cards.b: stop warfarin, IV vitamin K + FFP (or PCC)

cards.b: sterile necrosis doesn't automatically need intervention; deterioration → assess organ failure and intra-abdominal hypertension.

cards.f: Post-op PE?
cards.b: sudden hypoxaemia + hypotension with dilated RV and septal flattening → obstructive shock. Stable with high suspicion → CT pulmonary angiography (D-dimer is unhelpful post-op). Unstable with RV strain → supportive resuscitation, senior MDT input, assess bleeding risk for reperfusion; avoid large fluid volumes.

Just intubated → sudden desaturation, absent breath sounds on the RIGHT, high peak airway pressure
cards.b: right tension pneumothorax (a tube in the right main bronchus silences the LEFT side)
